title: NetOps Safety Testbed v1 — Integrated Generation→Verify→Emulate Benchmark (Preregistration)
research_question: Can a compact, public NetOps safety testbed combining intent-to-config generation, grammar-constrained decoding, formal verification, and emulation-execution metrics provide reproducible baseline measurements and expose recurrent failure modes of LLM-driven NetOps pipelines?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Constrained-decoding + verifier gating reduces the per-intent unsafe-change rate (absolute) by ≥10 percentage points compared with single-shot prompting (paired estimand).

H2: Iterative verifier-guided repair decreases residual unsafe-change rate relative to single-shot generation, but with diminishing returns after K=2 repair iterations; recurrent failure patterns will concentrate in a small set of categories (vendor-syntax, missing state, policy-violation).
exploratory_questions: E1: Which failure categories dominate across vendor clusters and prompting methods?
E2: How often do verifier false negatives (unsafe change accepted) occur compared with emulator-observed unsafe outcomes?
E3: What is the distribution of model-call cost vs. residual unsafe rate for the iterative repair method (cost-effectiveness frontier)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic, sanitized, multi-vendor intent set (abstracted CLI templates for four vendor-clusters: vendorA, vendorB, vendorC, vendorD).
End-to-end pipeline: generation → grammar/LMQL constraint → formal verifier (reachability + policy) → Mininet emulation execution → automatic rollback-cost metric.
Public artifacts limited to synthetic, redacted, template-based command sequences and machine-readable evaluation scripts (no real customer data).
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API endpoint available under the run capability (hosted_model_api_available).
Three prompting strategies applied to the hosted LLM: (1) single-shot baseline, (2) constrained-decoding (grammar/LMQL wrapper), (3) iterative verifier-guided repair (bound K=2).
transformation_scope: Intent → reference-config mapping via deterministic template expansion (synthetic state parameters).
Grammar-constrained decoding (LMQL-like) to enforce CLI token-level schema.
Automatic sanitizer transforming any detected sensitive tokens into abstract placeholders during dataset generation and output sanitization.
primary_estimand: Paired per-intent difference in unsafe-change indicator (unsafe after emulation execution) between constrained-decoding (method 2) and single-shot baseline (method 1).
secondary_estimands: Per-method residual unsafe rate after verifier gating (proportion of emulation runs producing unsafe outcome).
Average model-calls per successful safe configuration (cost-effectiveness).
Distribution (frequency) of failure categories across vendor clusters.
sampling_plan: Intent corpus: total 240 synthetic intents (200 confirmatory intents, 40 exploratory/adversarial intents). Confirmatory intents: balanced across four vendor-clusters (50 intents per cluster). For each intent we run three prompting strategies (methods 1–3). Per-intent per-method stochastic replicates: 3 independent generations (seeded). For iterative method (method 3) we allow up to K=2 repair iterations; average expected extra model calls per replicate assumed =1 (initial + avg 1 repair). Execution summary: total intents 240; confirmatory_items=200; discovery_items=40; task_cluster_count=4. Exact intent selection rules: all intents are synthetic, generated from abstracted templates with randomized but bounded parameters; inclusion excludes any template yielding direct-identifying tokens (IPs, customer names) via sanitization check. All seeds, template seeds, and generation RNGs will be recorded and published.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of unsafe-change proportions (per-intent paired indicator: unsafe after emulation for method A vs method B) between constrained-decoding and single-shot baseline using McNemar's test (paired binary outcomes) with alpha=0.05; report exact two-sided p-value and 95% confidence interval for paired risk difference. Secondary analyses: estimate residual unsafe rates (binomial CIs) per method; cost-effectiveness curves (model calls per safe outcome); failure-mode frequency counts and per-cluster contingency tables. Exploratory analyses: verifier false-negative rate (verifier accepted but emulation unsafe) and verifier false-positive rate (verifier rejected but emulation safe) reported descriptively. All tests and intervals computed with deterministic code (no manual adjudication). Pre-specified handling for nonconvergence (iterative method reaching K without verifier acceptance): count as 'nonconvergent' and include in intention-to-evaluate primary estimand as unsafe (conservative). All raw logs and hashes will be published.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory hypothesis: single pre-specified paired comparison (constrained-decoding vs single-shot) — controls multiplicity for the main claim. Secondary and exploratory tests are explicitly labeled exploratory; report unadjusted p-values and effect sizes. Where multiple secondary comparisons are reported, report Bonferroni-adjusted p-values in an appendix artifact.
missingness_plan: All failures to obtain model output (API error, timeout) are recorded as 'technical failure' and excluded from primary scientific analysis after transparent reporting; counts of excluded cases and reasons published. For iterative method runs aborted by infrastructure failure, the paired outcomes for that intent-method replicate will be marked missing and the whole intent replicate excluded from paired primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis using available-pair analysis will be reported. No human imputation or manual annotation is used.

risk_factors: Leakage of realistic/identifying command tokens in released artifacts.
Dataset contamination by unintentionally reusing real-world vendor-specific payloads.
Adversarially constructed intents that could be misused if too detailed.
detection_procedures: Regex-based scanners for IP addresses, domain names, email addresses, UUID patterns; any match triggers automatic redaction.
Entropy and token-pattern heuristics to flag sequences resembling real credentials or keys.
Deterministic template provenance tags embedded in every synthetic artifact; mismatched provenance flags rejection.
item_flagging_rules: If any regex detects an IP, domain, email, or credential-like token → automatically redact tokens and replace with safe placeholders before release.
If provenance tag is missing or malformed → exclude artifact from public release and place in internal 'quarantined' container for audit logs (not released).

If a generated output contains vendor CLI tokens not present in the sanitized template vocabulary → flag and exclude that replicate from public artifact set; include the replicate in internal logs for verifier analysis only.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are automatically excluded from public release; counts and reasons are published. For primary analyses, flagged items are excluded from the public confirmatory set (replacement intents from the same vendor-cluster drawn deterministically from the template seed pool to preserve sample size). All sanitization and redaction operations are deterministic and recorded.
residual_uncertainty: Sanitized synthetic templates may not perfectly reflect production CLI richness (external-validity limitation).
Automated detectors may have false negatives for novel sensitive formats (residual risk).

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal confirmatory pilot to validate pipeline and measure baseline unsafe rates with reduced scope.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Model-call budget 600 fits well within maximum_planned_model_calls=10000; uses 100 intents (80 confirmatory + 20 exploratory), two methods (single-shot + constrained-decoding), 3 replicates per intent → 100*2*3 = 600 model calls. Dockerized testbed and verifier run locally (CPU).

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended registered scenario: full preregistered benchmark run providing confirmatory power for primary estimand and richer exploratory coverage.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned model calls computed as: total intents 240 * 3 methods * 3 replicates per method * average calls factor for iterative method (method3 avg 2 calls per replicate) resulting in: method1 240*3=720, method2 240*3=720, method3 240*3*2=1440 → total 2880 model calls. This is ≤ the candidate estimated_model_calls (3000) and well under maximum_planned_model_calls (10000). All tooling packed in Docker with exact dependency versions for reproducible runs on CPU.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired per-intent difference in unsafe-change incidence between constrained-decoding and single-shot baseline.
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 10 percentage points (e.g., from 20% unsafe to 10% unsafe) in paired unsafe indicator.
power_plan.clustering_unit: Per-intent (each intent is a single cluster unit, paired across methods).
power_plan.calculation_method: Paired binary-outcome power approximation using McNemar/paired proportion reasoning with conservative variance approximation. Approximated sample-size calculation: (Z_{1-α/2}+Z_{1-β})^2 * (p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)) / (Δ^2) with α=0.05, power=0.8; for p1=0.20, p2=0.10, Δ=0.10 → n≈196. Accounting for paired design and potential exclusions, we preregister confirmatory n=200 intents.
assumptions: Paired correlation between methods moderate (assumed 0.5) — this reduces required n relative to unpaired calculation; we use conservative unpaired-equivalent calculation then set n=200 to be robust.
Per-intent replicates = 3 stochastic generations reduce within-intent measurement noise; primary analysis collapses replicates to per-method per-intent unsafe indicator via logical OR.
Nonconvergent iterative runs are counted as unsafe (conservative).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 paired confirmatory intents, the preregistered design targets an MDE of ~10 percentage points under conservative variance assumptions; smaller effects (e.g., 5%) are underpowered in this budget and would require substantially larger confirmatory sets (>700 intents).
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute paired effect CIs under assumptions of lower baseline unsafe rate (15%) and higher rate (25%).
Perform per-cluster power checks (n≈50 intents per vendor-cluster) and report clusterwise effect estimates with wider CIs (exploratory).
Report results under two treatments for nonconvergence: (A) conservative (count as unsafe) and (B) available-pair analysis (exclude missing pairs).

transformation_families: Grammar-constrained decoding (LMQL-like) to enforce token-level CLI schema.
Automated sanitizer/redactor transforming detected sensitive tokens to placeholders.
semantic_equivalence_checks: Unit tests in emulation: for each generated config, run deterministic Mininet-based execution and assert reachability and policy predicates defined by the intent; outcomes are binary (pass/fail).
Verifier cross-check: formal verifier run prior to emulation to check reachability/policy; verifier output compared with emulation outcome to quantify verifier false-negative/false-positive rates.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject (exclude from public release) any generated config that fails grammar parse or contains redacted placeholders left unresolved.

If verifier rejects config but emulation shows safety, retain for diagnostic logs only (not used to claim safe outcome); if verifier accepts but emulation detects unsafe outcome, mark as verifier false-negative for analysis.

If sanitizer detects sensitive-token patterns in an output, automatically redact and re-run generation with adjusted template; if repeated, exclude that replicate and deterministically replace intent from seed pool.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deterministic audit: 5% of all generated outputs (stratified by vendor-cluster and method) are subject to additional static-analysis heuristics (pattern matching, grammar trees) and full verifier→emulation cross-checks to validate automation pipelines; audit selection and results are fully reproducible and published.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Deterministic intent→reference-config mapping code is unit-tested; reference configs embedded in the dataset are generated by the same template engine and validated in Mininet before inclusion.
residual_risks: Emulator fidelity may not capture all vendor-specific runtime quirks (residual coverage gap).
Grammar constraints enforce surface syntax but do not guarantee semantic correctness under all vendor semantics.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External validity: synthetic, template-based intents may not capture full production CLI heterogeneity; conclusions explicitly bounded to synthetic benchmark scope.
Verifier false negatives: formal verifier coverage is limited to declared predicates (reachability, simple policy); complex device behaviors may elude checks.
Emulation fidelity: Mininet-based emulation abstracts vendor hardware and OS-level quirks; emulation may under- or over-estimate real-world unsafe outcomes.
Single hosted LLM endpoint: results do not generalize to other model families or vendors absent further evaluation.
